finderFindings.claim: New exported SGroupDialogResult duplicates an identical local interface that already exists in sgroup.ts.
finderFindings.scenario: The diff adds `export interface SGroupDialogResult { type?: string; attrs: {...} }` at Editor.types.ts:33, but sgroup.ts:43 already declares the same shape as a local interface and keeps using it at sgroup.ts:799 and :855. Two copies of the shape now exist. If the dialog result gains a field, the Editor.event.sgroupEdit type (Editor.ts:301) and the sgroup.ts handler can drift apart. Importing the exported type into sgroup.ts and deleting its local copy would give one definition.

finderFindings.claim: `?? null` coerces undefined at the call site to fit the callee's parameter type.
finderFindings.scenario: `fromRGroupAttachmentPointUpdate` declares `attachmentPoints: AttachmentPoints | null` (rgroupAttachmentPoint.ts:15). The caller's `currentAttachmentPoints` is `AttachmentPoints | undefined`, so the diff patches the call site with `?? null` instead of stating the type the caller really has. The next caller hits the same mismatch and copies the coalescing. Widen the callee parameter to accept `undefined`, or fix the caller's type where it is declared.

finderFindings.claim: The `elementEdit` result type is declared twice with different shapes, and the copies have diverged.
finderFindings.scenario: The core `IEditorEvents.elementEdit` is `PipelineSubscription<unknown, Promise<Partial<AtomAttributes>>>`, while the react `Editor.event.elementEdit` uses the new `ElementEditResult = Partial<AtomAttributes> & { content?: string }`. Code that reads the result through the core interface cannot see `content`, and code that reads it through the react type can. Keep one exported type and reference it from both places, so a field added to one result cannot go missing from the other.

finderFindings.claim: `BondEditResult` is a pure alias of `Bond` that adds a name and no shape.
finderFindings.scenario: `export type BondEditResult = Bond;` only renames `Bond`, and it is used once, in `bondEdit: PipelineSubscription<Bond[], Promise<BondEditResult>>` (Editor.ts:305). A reader has to check whether the alias hides a different shape. Use `Bond` directly.

finderFindings.claim: Widening `editorEvents` to `Record<keyof IEditorEvents, Subscription>` erases each event's payload type to make the write compile.
finderFindings.scenario: `resetEditorEvents` now writes through `Record<keyof IEditorEvents, Subscription>`, so every key accepts any `Subscription`, and the per-event generics (e.g. `selectMonomer: Subscription<MonomerItemType>`) are no longer checked on reset. A reset that assigns the wrong subscription type to a key compiles silently. Use a typed mapping helper, or keep the declared type and confine the single widening to one place.

confirmed.claim: The `elementEdit` result type is declared twice with different shapes, and the copies have diverged.
confirmed.scenario: The core `Editor` interface types the `elementEdit` result as `Partial<AtomAttributes>`. The react `Editor` types it as `Partial<AtomAttributes> & { content?: string }`. A caller that reads the result through the core interface cannot see `content`. A new field added to one type can be missing from the other. The react type is a subset-compatible superset, so nothing breaks today, which makes this a drift risk and not a bug.

confirmed.claim: `BondEditResult` is a pure alias of `Bond` that adds a name and no shape.
confirmed.scenario: `BondEditResult` is defined as `Bond` and imported once. The only use is the `bondEdit` subscription type, which sits at Editor.ts:299 and not line 305. A reader has to open Editor.types.ts to learn that it is just `Bond`. The type could be `Promise<Bond>` there. The alias does match the naming of the sibling result types.

confirmed.claim: New exported SGroupDialogResult duplicates an identical local interface that already exists in sgroup.ts.
confirmed.scenario: The diff adds an exported SGroupDialogResult in Editor.types.ts:33. sgroup.ts:43 already declares an identical local interface and uses it at lines 799, 855 and 937. There are now two definitions that can drift apart. sgroup.ts could import the exported type and drop its local copy.
